nodes.label: Worsening dyspnea on exertion for 2 months
65-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity
Medications included lisinopril, aspirin, and atorvastatin
Physical examination showed vital signs within normal limits and unremarkable cardiac and respiratory examinations
Echocardiography shows preserved LVEF without wall motion abnormalities
Exercise ECG shows dynamic QRS widening and new T-wave inversions in recovery
Echocardiography shows sclerotic aortic valve with mild regurgitation
Exertional dyspnea is caused by coronary artery disease with exercise-induced myocardial ischemia
Coronary angiography or myocardial perfusion imaging was requested but no results are available
Aortic valve sclerosis with mild regurgitation contributes to exertional dyspnea
Coronary artery disease with exercise-induced myocardial ischemia
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
Aortic valve sclerosis with hemodynamically significant regurgitation as primary cause
Coronary artery disease with exercise-induced myocardial ischemia
